solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Lack of trust in my CIC's disastrous

indicators.note: a disastrous arrangement is one wrecked and thrown into disorder, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: the letters C, I, C and S are used as printed

explanation.surface: Someone complains that their commander-in-chief's catastrophic failure has destroyed their faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disastrous' rearranges IN + MY + CICS; CIC (commander-in-chief) is only fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Cynicism is a habitual distrust of other people's motives, which is a lack of trust.

clue.text: Stars who may become despicable if not paid

indicators.note: says the letters of the word despicable can be rearranged into something else
signals that the letters of the word paid are taken away from the pool before rearranging

explanation.surface: Famous people who go unpaid may turn nasty.
explanation.walkthrough: Composite anagram: 'may become' rearranges DESPICABLE once 'if not' has removed P, A, I, D, leaving six letters to shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Celebs is short for celebrities, people who are stars in the entertainment world.

clue.text: Resort to extremely trendy refinement

parts.note: Nice is a resort city on the French Riviera

indicators.note: points to the two extreme letters, first and last, of the word trendy

explanation.surface: A smart resort is advertised as the height of fashionable sophistication.
explanation.definitionFit: A nicety is a fine detail or subtle point of etiquette, a refinement.

clue.text: Reserved utter evacuation of rodents

parts.note: coy means shy or reserved

indicators.note: to utter is to say aloud, so the word for evacuation is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: poo is a colloquial word for an evacuation of the bowels

explanation.surface: Shy animals are being completely cleared out of somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'utter' looks like an adjective meaning complete; it is the instruction to say POO aloud, written PU.
explanation.definitionFit: Coypu are large South American water rodents; the plural is often the same as the singular.

clue.text: Boy plunges back in Galway Bay

indicators.note: read back means the whole run of letters from the two pieces is taken from right to left

parts.note: a lad is a boy
dips means plunges, as into water

explanation.surface: A young lad dives back into the sea off the west coast of Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses both pieces together, not just the second. Spiddal is a little-known village, so the wordplay has to carry the solve.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiddal is a village on the north shore of Galway Bay in the west of Ireland, a place found there.

clue.text: Jumped ship — initiated collision

indicators.note: something initiated is begun, so only the start of the word ship is used

parts.note: prang is British slang for a minor crash or collision

explanation.surface: A sailor abandoned ship after it was involved in a crash.
explanation.walkthrough: PRANG is British slang for a minor crash, especially in a car or aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprang is the past tense of spring, meaning leapt or jumped.

clue.text: Scrap watch maybe one with fewer hours

parts.note: a scrap is a piece or part
a watch is one example of a timer

explanation.surface: Someone discards a watch, perhaps because they now work fewer hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrap' looks like a verb, to throw away; it is the noun, a bit.
explanation.definitionFit: A part-timer is a worker whose contract has fewer hours than a full-time employee's.

clue.text: Involved in detaching Lycra with great pain

indicators.note: the answer is involved in, contained within, the run of letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Peeling off tight Lycra sportswear can be agonising.
explanation.definitionFit: Achingly is the adverb from aching, meaning in a way that hurts, with great pain.

clue.text: Throttle opens to get air roaring right on to the engine

indicators.note: the openings, the first letters, of each of the following words are taken

explanation.surface: Instructions on revving a motor: open the throttle so air roars into the engine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throttle' reads as an engine part; it is the verb, to strangle.
explanation.definitionFit: To garrotte is to strangle someone with a cord or wire, to throttle them.

clue.text: Brave princess first to end speculation

indicators.note: the opening letter of the assembled words is shifted to the end

parts.note: plucky means brave
Di was the popular name of Diana, Princess of Wales

explanation.surface: A courageous princess comes first in some race or contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first to end' moves P from the front of PLUCKYDI to the back. A lucky dip is a British fairground game: a tub you reach into for a random prize.
explanation.definitionFit: A lucky dip is a random choice whose outcome is uncertain, a gamble or speculation.

clue.text: Ruler with an inner circle

parts.note: a king whose closest knights sat around a famous round table, an inner circle in both senses

explanation.surface: A leader who relies on a close group of trusted advisers.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary British king's knights met at the Round Table, literally a circle of insiders.

clue.text: Nearly injure small reptile

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: to crock is to injure or disable, as in a crocked footballer

explanation.surface: An unlucky encounter where a little lizard is almost hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: Croc is the short form of crocodile, so 'small' signals the abbreviated reptile.

clue.text: Curse how one is deafened

definitions.meaning: an old-fashioned oath or exclamation of surprise
the means by which a loud storm might leave someone unable to hear

explanation.surface: Swearing at a noise so loud it has made one deaf.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a mild oath, and literally names the loud crash of a storm that could deafen.

clue.text: Dance holidaymaker sees eventually

parts.note: a whimsical hint: what a sunbather finds in time is that the colour they acquired fades, the tan will go

explanation.surface: A tourist finally watches some local dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: No strict wordplay: the rest of the clue playfully splits the answer as TAN GO, what a holidaymaker eventually sees happen to their suntan.
explanation.definitionFit: The tango is a ballroom dance that originated in Argentina.

clue.text: Delivery round

definitions.meaning: in cricket a single delivery by the bowler is called this

explanation.surface: Something round being delivered.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket bowler's delivery is one bowled throw; and a sphere is a round object.

clue.text: Where swinging sailors hate to see drag

definitions.text: Where swinging sailors hate to see drag

parts.words: Where swinging sailors hate to see drag
parts.note: a moored ship swings around its anchor; sailors fear the anchor dragging along the seabed

explanation.surface: It sounds like broad-minded seafarers who disapprove of cross-dressing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swinging' and 'drag' suggest a racy nightlife; here a ship swings at its mooring and an anchor may drag.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a place where ships lie at anchor, swinging with tide and wind.

clue.text: Legendary court order for meal in bed

indicators.note: one piece is placed within the bed word

parts.note: a cot is a small bed

indicators.note: to put in order is to arrange, so the letters of the following word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone requests room service: a meal to be eaten in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order for' reads as placing an order for food, but it is the instruction to rearrange the word after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Camelot was the legendary castle and court of the Arthurian knights.

clue.text: Janus the Italian in battle of huge numbers

indicators.note: the two-way piece goes inside the battle

parts.note: Mons was a First World War battle in Belgium, in 1914
il is the Italian for 'the'

indicators.note: the Roman god Janus has two faces looking in opposite directions, so the word is shown forwards and also backwards

parts.note: the same Italian article, read the other way

explanation.surface: A two-faced god leads an Italian army to a battle of vast scale.
explanation.walkthrough: The Roman god Janus has two faces, so 'Janus' writes the Italian article facing forwards and then backwards. Mons was a 1914 battle in Belgium.
explanation.definitionFit: Millions is an informal way of saying vast quantities, huge numbers of things.

clue.text: 23 has bats

definitions.meaning: the answer to 23 is someone who places wagers, so this is what such a person has: small bets
bats as with eyelashes, flickering them quickly

explanation.surface: The cross-reference gives a gambler and some flying mammals.
explanation.walkthrough: 23 is a BETTER, a person who bets; in British slang a flutter is a small bet.
explanation.definitionFit: A flutter is a small bet, and to flutter eyelashes is to bat them.

clue.text: It's about 50-50 chemists were unlicensed

indicators.note: the word it goes about, around, the other pieces

parts.note: the letters I and T as printed
L is the Roman numeral for fifty, so fifty twice gives two Ls
ICI was Imperial Chemical Industries, a British chemicals company

explanation.surface: Pharmacists illegally operating had an even chance of getting away with it.
explanation.walkthrough: '50-50' looks like even odds; it is two Roman fifties. 'were' hints that ICI no longer exists, having been taken over in 2008.
explanation.definitionFit: Illicit means forbidden by law, done without permission, so unlicensed.

clue.text: Received backing over second hand garment

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece is over, placed above, the next
going backwards, so the received word is turned round

parts.note: got means received

indicators.note: the second letter of the word hand

explanation.surface: Someone was given a used, second-hand piece of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns GOT into TOG; 'second' takes A, the second letter of hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A toga was the loose outer robe worn by citizens of ancient Rome, a garment.

clue.text: Mark's successor in Richelieu role

indicators.note: the answer sits in the letters of the following words

explanation.surface: An actor takes over the part of Cardinal Richelieu from someone named Mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a name; it is the Deutschmark, Germany's currency before 2002.
explanation.definitionFit: The single European currency replaced the German mark, so it is the mark's successor.

clue.text: State old musicians value

parts.note: EMI was a long-established British record company, the label of many musicians
to rate is to value or assess

explanation.surface: A statement that veteran musicians deserve appreciation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a verb; it is the noun, a country.
explanation.definitionFit: An emirate is a country ruled by an emir, such as those in the Gulf, so a state.

clue.text: Gaff hands in bird of prey

parts.note: Gaff is this puzzle's setter, so the setter refers to himself as me
the right and left hands give R and L

explanation.surface: A gaff is a hook, so a bird of prey being hooked or handled.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often use their own pseudonym for ME.
explanation.definitionFit: A merlin is a small falcon, a bird of prey.

clue.text: Superior ale-houses having no alcohol

indicators.note: to house is to contain, so the ale word holds the other piece

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer
TT means teetotal, abstaining from alcohol

explanation.surface: Pubs that serve no alcohol are claimed to be superior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ale-houses' looks like pubs; split it into 'ale' and 'houses', and the second word becomes the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Better is the comparative of good, meaning of higher quality, superior.

clue.text: John claims race is a gamble

indicators.note: to claim is to take hold of, so the john word holds the other piece

parts.note: john and loo are both slang for a toilet
the TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A man named John says a horse race is just a gamble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'John' looks like a name; it is slang for a toilet, LOO in British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A lotto is a lottery, a game of chance and so a gamble.

clue.text: Half a beer always starts embarrassing queen

indicators.note: the first half of the beer's name is used

parts.note: Guinness is a famous Irish stout, a beer
ever means always

indicators.note: the start of the following word is used

explanation.surface: Someone half-drunk on beer is perpetually embarrassing the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half' takes GUIN from GUINNESS; 'starts' gives E from embarrassing.
explanation.definitionFit: Guinevere was the legendary queen, wife of King Arthur.

clue.text: Shine from church at first light

parts.note: ex is Latin for from, as in ex-works
CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: only the first letter of the following word is used

explanation.surface: A glow comes from a church at dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'light' looks like the definition next to 'Shine'; only its first letter, L, is used.
explanation.definitionFit: To excel is to stand out by being very good, to shine at something.

clue.text: In the end, authority wastes money building traffic scheme

indicators.note: building is putting together, so the letters are assembled into a new arrangement
only the end letter of the word authority is used

explanation.surface: A council squanders cash constructing a new road layout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the end' gives Y from authority; 'building' rearranges Y + WASTES + MONEY.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-way system is a traffic scheme where cars may go in only one direction on certain streets.

clue.text: Knight who was terribly tall once

indicators.note: terribly means badly, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A knight who used to be extremely tall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' looks like an intensifier for 'tall'; it rearranges TALL ONCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Lancelot was the foremost knight of the Round Table in Arthurian legend.

clue.text: See 27
Chair person adjusts to many positions

definitions.text: Chair person adjusts to many positions

parts.words: Chair person adjusts to many positions
parts.note: a seat whose back can be adjusted into many positions

explanation.surface: It looks like a chairperson who is very flexible about views.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chair person' looks like a meeting's chair; it is an armchair you adjust.
explanation.definitionFit: A recliner is an armchair with a back that tilts to various angles for relaxing.
